My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 10 mu. My children all moved to Shijiazhuang and Handan years ago. I manage the fields mostly alone, sometimes I pay a neighbor's son to help with the heavy work.

I do not think much about changing what I grow. Everyone here grows wheat in winter and corn in summer, on the same land. It has been this way my whole life. The wheat brings steady money and we need it for flour. The corn sells well too, or I can feed it to my daughter-in-law's family pigs when they visit.

For wheat I will buy improved seed from the village seed station — I stopped saving my own seed maybe 10 years ago because the station seed gives better yield. For corn I always buy hybrid, same brand as my neighbor Old Wang uses, Zhengdan 958. It never fails badly.

I will plough the field before wheat, as I have always done. For corn after the wheat harvest, the ground is already loose enough so I just do rotary tillage — it is faster and my back is not what it was.

I apply compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the wheat is jointing. Same pattern my husband taught me. I do not reduce fertilizer — if I put less, maybe the yield drops and then what. I irrigate the wheat three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Corn I irrigate twice if it is dry at emergence and again at tasseling, but I skip if rain comes.

I spray herbicide on the wheat in early spring and a fungicide spray before harvest because the extension station truck came by last year and said powdery mildew was bad. Corn I spray once for stem borer around July.
